info.title: RoboDE Studio API
info.summary: Design a rough robot from a task, then find and check real robots that can do the job.
info.description:
The HTTP API of RoboDE Studio. Everything the web app does goes through these routes, so another application can
drive every feature: brief, reference files, question rounds (with comments, notes and answer images), design,
versions and assets, revise (base version, moment, auto repair), approve, fleet, catalog search, datasheet
analysis, decision, export, jobs, and LLM settings and usage.

This file is the authoritative spec for every `/api/v1` route. Java tests check that each route has an entry here,
and that every JSON response of the flow tests validates against its schema. Domain types (`DesignVersion`,
`Candidate`, `Analysis`, ...) are the generated JSON Schemas in `contracts/schemas/`; their single source is the
pydantic models in `server/studio/schemas.py`. `contracts/openapi.bundled.json` is this file with every reference
resolved; the server serves it at `GET /api/v1/openapi.json`, and other languages can generate an SDK from it.

## Units and frames
- SI units: metres, kilograms, seconds, newtons, newton-metres, watt-hours. Angles are radians in data (joint
  values in frames, `BasePose.yaw`) and degrees only where a field name says so (for example `j1_max_deg`).
- World frame: z up, origin on the floor, x and y in metres. A family works in its base frame (origin at the
  mounting point, x axis along `BasePose.yaw`).
- GLB assets and the three.js client are y up (a rotation of -90 degrees about X from the world frame).
- Timestamps are UTC ISO 8601 strings. `t` in a revise request is seconds into a version's simulation.

## Jobs
Design, revise, fleet design, search, analysis and the LLM profile test are jobs. The start call returns a job
record (status `running`) and the result is read from `GET /jobs/{id}`. Instead of polling, pass `wait=<seconds>`
to the start call or to `GET /jobs/{id}`: if the job ends in time the answer is 200 with the final record,
otherwise 202 with the running record and a `Location` header. `expand=resource` adds the result as a full
resource (for example the new design version). `X-Studio-Callback: <url>` registers a signed POST to your app when
the job ends. `DELETE /jobs/{id}` cancels a running job (status `cancelled`, `error_code` `cancelled`). A project runs one design,
revise or fleet design job at a time (409 otherwise), and one studio build at a time. Starting a search, or an analysis of the same candidate,
while one is running returns the running job.

## Idempotency
`POST /projects` and every job-starting POST accept `Idempotency-Key` (1 to 200 characters). Keys are kept in
memory for 24 hours, per key, method and path. The same key with the same body replays the stored response as it was (status,
body and headers: same project, same job id; a stored 202 replays as 202); responses of 500 and above are not
stored; the same key with a different body, or an empty or over-long key, is a 422. The key check reads at most 4 MB of
body (413 above that). A server restart forgets all keys.

## Errors
Every error body is `{"detail": string, "error_code"?: string}`. Status codes: 401 (token missing or wrong),
404 (unknown project, version, candidate, job or route), 409 (state conflict: project busy, approved design is
frozen), 413 (upload above 64 MB), 422 (invalid input), 502 (the language model failed) and 500. A job that fails
keeps the HTTP status 200 and reports `status: "error"` with `error` and `error_code` (for example
`datasheet_download`) in its record.

## Authentication
The server binds to 127.0.0.1 by default, and loopback callers need no credentials. With `STUDIO_TOKEN` set
(required for any other bind address), every `/api/v1` call needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The scheme is
therefore declared optional (`security: [{}, {bearerAuth: []}]`): none on an open loopback server, bearer
otherwise.

## Versioning policy
`/api/v1` is additive only: new routes, new optional request fields and new response fields may appear, but no
route, field or enum value is removed or changes meaning. A client must ignore response fields it does not
know. Breaking changes go to `/api/v2`.

## Limits
A project brief is 1 to 8000 characters. Uploads are at most 64 MB. At most 8 reference plus answer images go to
the model per design round. The server runs at most 4 task processes at once.

put.description: Replaces the reference text. An empty string removes it. Photos and the URDF are kept.

delete.summary: Remove the whole reference (text, photos, URDF)

put.description:
Replaces the brief (10 to 20000 characters after trimming). Pending questions are cleared and `round` resets to
0, so the next design call starts the question rounds again with the new brief. Earlier answers, comments and
notes are kept; existing versions are untouched. `brief_updated` is set. 409 when a version is approved
or while a design or revise job runs for the project.

post.summary: Attach a photo to the brief
post.description:
Raw image bytes (PNG, JPEG or WebP): a photo of the task, the objects or the workcell (not the reference robot).
Brief, reference and answer images together are at most 8 (422 beyond). Not allowed after a version is approved (409).
The images go to the model with the next design call.

200.description: All brief images of the project.
The image bytes with their detected media type.

delete.description: Not allowed after a version is approved (409).

post.summary: Upload a reference photo or URDF
post.description:
Raw file bytes as the body. PNG, JPEG or WebP photos (at most 6 per project, and 8 images in all with brief and
answer images) or a `.urdf` / `.zip` robot description (replaces the previous one). The file is inspected before it is stored.

post.summary: Run the next design step (question round or design)
post.description:
Starts a design job. The AI either returns the next round of questions (`result.status: questions`) or, when
it has enough answers, the first design version (`result.status: designed`, `result.version`). Send the answers
given so far (new answers are merged into the project's answers), optional comments per question, one general
note per round, and images attached with `uploadAnswerImage`.

200.description: The job record (running, or finished when `wait` was used and the job ended in time).

post.summary: Attach an image to a question
post.description:
Raw image bytes (PNG, JPEG or WebP). `question` is a question id of the current round or `_general` for the
round's note. Images are sent to the model with the next design call.

200.description: All answer images of the project.
The image bytes with their detected media type.

get.description: The stored version (spec, requirements, scene, robot, URDF, simulation with frames and checks) plus the parsed URDF.
`design.urdf` (the robot, XML), `design.glb` (zero-pose mesh, glTF binary, y up) or `frames.json` (the simulated frames).

post.summary: Approve (freeze) a version
post.description: Freezes the design. Approving the approved version again is a no-op; approving another version is a 409.

post.summary: Change a design by a request
post.description:
Starts a revise job that creates a new version from `base_version` (default: the latest). `t` is the moment
of the base version's simulation the request refers to, in seconds (0 up to its duration). The result is
`{version: n}`. A project with an approved version is frozen (409).

put.description: Stores the manual baseline and the working pattern used by the time-saved estimate (any subset of the fields; `null` removes `manual_cycle_s` or `operators`, or restores another field's default). Stored values override `spec.baseline` and the defaults. Allowed while a design or revise job runs. The estimate itself is computed from these inputs and the robot's simulated cycle (`savings` in `@robode/studio-core`); it is not a time study.
Turn the fleet on or off, set its limits (`null` clears them) and choose the member used for robot search. Send at least one field.

post.summary: Preview and store a robot assignment
post.description:
Runs immediately (no AI, no job). With no `assignment` the code proposes one; with an `assignment` it is
validated and stored as the user's confirmed assignment. The base version defaults to the approved version,
else the latest.

200.description: The assignment, a preview of the layout, and whether it is feasible.

post.summary: Plan the fleet as a new version
post.description: Starts a fleet_design job on the base version (default: the latest) using the stored assignment. 409 when no assignment was stored or the design is approved.

200.description: The job record. The result is `{version: n}`.

post.summary: Search for real robots that fit the approved design
post.description: Starts a search job (the design must be approved, otherwise the job ends with an error). While a search of the project is running the same job record is returned. The result is `{candidates: [...]}`.

get.summary: List the candidates found by the last search

post.summary: Analyse a candidate against its datasheet
post.description:
Starts an analyse job. The datasheet comes from, in order: `datasheet_url` (https only), a datasheet uploaded
with `uploadDatasheet`, the candidate's own datasheet link, its product page. Quotes are verified against the
document text. The same candidate being analysed returns the running job. The result is the analysis view
(`GET /projects/{pid}/analysis/{cid}`). A failed download ends the job with `error_code: datasheet_download`.

post.summary: Upload a datasheet for a candidate
post.description: Raw bytes of a PDF, HTML or text file. It is used by the next analysis of this candidate that has no `datasheet_url`.

get.summary: Read the analysis of a candidate

200.description: The analysis with the parsed URDF of the candidate's robot.

post.summary: Record the decision
post.description: Either choose an analysed catalog candidate, or choose your own design (the approved Robot studio build). Choosing again overwrites the decision. `self` returns 409 when no build is approved (or the given build is not approved) and 404 for an unknown build.

self.summary: Build our own design (the approved Robot studio build)

get.summary: Export the design as a zip
get.description: The approved version (else the latest) with spec, requirements, scene, simulation summary, URDF, GLB, every analysis and the decision, and a README of the limits.

post.summary: Build the robot (CAD, motors, electronics)
post.description:
Starts a `studio_build` job for the approved design version. `design_version` defaults to the approved one and
must be it (409 otherwise, and 409 while no version is approved). `base_build` starts from an earlier build;
with only `pinned` changed (`{joint: alternative_id}`) the shop search is not repeated. `request` is a change
in words. Only one studio build runs per project at a time (409). The result is `{build: n}`; with
`expand=resource` the job carries the build view. Sizing and CAD checks are kinematic and static calculations,
not dynamics and not hardware tests; prices are dated web estimates.

200.description: The job record (running, or finished when `wait` was used and the job ended in time).

get.summary: List the builds of a project

get.description: The stored build (sizing, motors, electronics, style, parts, URDF, twin limits, checks, files) plus the parsed studio URDF.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: A relative path inside the build folder, for example `assembly.step` or `parts/p1.stl`. Paths that leave the folder are a 422.

get.summary: Download a file of a build
get.description: STEP is `model/step`, STL `model/stl`, URDF `application/xml`; also PNG, PDF, ZIP, CSV and JSON.

post.summary: Move the digital twin to a target
post.description:
Runs the twin synchronously (no model): from `q0` to joint values or a cartesian point under the build's joint,
speed, acceleration and torque limits. The result lists the frames and every limit that bound. This is a
kinematic and limit model, not a dynamics simulation.

post.summary: Replay the design's task on the twin
post.description: Replays the design's waypoints under the build's limits (synchronous, no model).

post.summary: Store a render of the twin
post.description: The raw PNG body (at most 15 MB) is stored for the manufacturer PDF. A build that is approved is frozen (409). A body that is not a PNG is a 422.

200.description: The views stored for this build.

post.summary: Approve a build and make the manufacturer package
post.description: Starts a `studio_pdf` job (no model) that writes `manufacturer.pdf`, `package.zip` and `bom.csv`, then marks the build approved. The result is `{build: n}`. An approved build is a 409.

get.description: Available once the build is approved; 404 before.
A ZIP with the PDF, assembly STEP, parts, URDF and BOM CSV. Available once the build is approved; 404 before.

post.summary: Ask a question about the project on screen
post.description: Starts an `ask` job (role `ask`). The server builds the facts to answer from for the ids in `context` (project, version, build, candidate, the moment `t`) from stored data: numbers are never taken from the client. The model answers from those facts and may propose at most two actions of a fixed list (`revise`, `design`, `search`, `analyse`, `studio_build`, `update_brief`, `set_baseline`, `cancel_job`). The server validates each proposal exactly as the matching route validates its body, executes it (a job it starts appears in the project's job list and can be cancelled) and reports it in `actions_taken`; a refused one has `ok: false` and an `error` (`not allowed` for anything else, such as delete, keys, settings, profiles, approve or decision; `limit: 2 actions per question` for extras). An approval, a build approval or a decision is never executed: it comes back in `confirm` as a chip whose `request` is the body of the existing route (`approve_build` also carries `build`, which goes into the path). Each action is logged in the project's activity. `navigate` only tells the client where to look. 404 when a referenced project, version, build or candidate does not exist; 422 for an invalid body.

get.description:
Jobs are kept in memory (the last finished ones), so a job id is unknown after a server restart. With
`wait`, the call returns as soon as the job ends (200) or after the wait with the running record (202).

200.description: The job record (running, done, error or cancelled).

questions.summary: A finished design job that asked questions

designed.summary: A finished design job that produced version 1

progress: Working out what the change touches

value.error: Datasheet download failed: Only https:// URLs are allowed. Upload the datasheet (PDF or text) instead.

delete.description:
Kills the job's task process tree. The record becomes `status: cancelled` with `error` "Cancelled by the caller" and `error_code` `cancelled`. The call waits up to 10 seconds for the processes to stop. If a task finishes at the very moment of the cancel it may already have committed, and the record still says cancelled.
Model usage already streamed is kept; nothing is committed to the project from a cancelled job; the project
lock is released. A job that already ended is a 409.

get.description: Running jobs first (oldest first), then finished ones (newest first), at most 20, with `subject` and `finished`.
Profiles, the profile of each role, the provider kinds, API key status and the models each kind offers. LLM connections are global, not per project. API keys are never returned.

post.summary: Add a profile

delete.description: A profile that a role uses cannot be deleted (422).

post.summary: Test a profile with a small request
post.description: Starts an `llm_test` job. Its result is `{ok, answer, seconds}`.

put.description: Planner and converter style roles (`spec`, `scene`, `robot`, `revise`, `search`, `extract`, `analysis`) can use different profiles. Roles not in the body keep their profile.

200.description: The profile id of every role.

put.description: The key is stored on the server and never returned.

post.summary: Start a new usage ledger
post.description: The old ledger is kept on the server beside the new one.

get.description: The shops the user wants searched first for robots, motors and electronics. A global setting, not part of a project.

200.description: The saved vendors (an empty list when none were saved).

put.description:
Replaces the whole list (at most 50). Each domain is a bare host such as `robu.in` (lower case, no scheme or path);
domains must be unique. Catalog searches and studio builds started afterwards use the new list.

bearerAuth.description:
Required only when the server runs with `STUDIO_TOKEN` (always for a non-loopback bind). Loopback callers of an
unprotected server send nothing. A wrong or missing token is a 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`.

ProjectId.name: pid
ProjectId.description: Project id, as returned by `createProject` (`p_` and 10 hex characters).

CandidateId.name: cid
CandidateId.description: Candidate id from the search result.

Provider.name: provider
Provider.description: A provider kind that needs a key, for example `gemini`.

Filename.name: filename
Filename.description: Name of the uploaded file. Its extension tells the type (for example `photo.png`, `robot.urdf`, `ra6.pdf`).

Wait.name: wait
Wait.description:
Whole seconds to wait for the job to end (0 to 600; outside that range is a 422). 0 returns at once. If the job ends within the wait the answer
is 200 with the final record, otherwise 202 with the running record.

Expand.name: expand
Expand.description: `resource` (the only value; others are a 422) adds the job's result as a full resource in `resource` once the job is finished (see `Job.resource`).

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description:
1 to 200 characters. The same key with the same body replays the first response; with a different body it is a
422 (as is an empty or longer key). A replay returns the stored status, body and headers; 500 and above are not stored. Kept in
memory for 24 hours per key, method and path.

Callback.name: X-Studio-Callback
Callback.description:
http(s) URL that receives the final job record (expanded) as a POST when the job ends (done, error or
cancelled), with `X-Studio-Job`, `X-Studio-Event: job.finished` and, when `STUDIO_CALLBACK_SECRET` is set,
`X-Studio-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC of the body>`. Up to four attempts (at once, then after 1, 5 and 25 seconds; `callback.attempts` counts them all); a failed
delivery never changes the job. A search or analysis that joins a running job keeps the first callback URL. The host must be in `STUDIO_CALLBACK_HOSTS` (default `localhost,127.0.0.1,::1`),
otherwise the start is a 422.

JobRunning.description: The job did not end within `wait`. The running record; poll `Location` or wait again.

Unauthorized.description: The server needs a bearer token and none, or a wrong one, was sent.

example.detail: A valid bearer token is required

NotFound.description: Unknown project, version, candidate, job, profile or file.

Conflict.description: State conflict, for example the project is busy with another design step, the approved design is frozen, or the job already ended.

example.detail: This project is still working on another design step

TooLarge.description: The upload is above 64 MB (a multipart size error gives the same body), or the body checked for an Idempotency-Key is above 4 MB.

Unprocessable.description: The input is not acceptable (missing or malformed field, unsafe URL, Idempotency-Key reuse, bad callback host).

error_code.description: Machine-readable cause when there is one, for example `datasheet_download`.

params_schema.description: JSON Schema of the family parameters.

Stage.description: Where the project is. `brief` (created), `questions` (a round awaits answers), `designed`, `approved`, `candidates` (search done), `analysed`, `decided`.

Reference.description: The reference text and files; null when there is none.

BriefImage.description: A photo attached to the brief (task, objects or workcell).

brief.description: The new brief (10 to 20000 characters after trimming).

AnswerImage.description: An image attached to an answer (a question id, or `_general` for the round's note).

FleetState.description: Present on a project only when a fleet was suggested or the user changed fleet settings.

source.description: One of spec, code, both, user.

member.description: The member used for robot search and analysis.

DecisionRecord.description: The recorded decision: a catalog candidate (`approve`, or the legacy `robot_studio`) or your own design (`self`, with the build number); null before a decision.

answers.description: Answers so far, by question id.

brief_updated.description: Only once the brief has been edited.

analyses.description: Candidate ids that have an analysis.

answers.description: Answers by question id (string, number, boolean or list).

comments.description: A comment per question id (lower case letters, digits and underscore, at most 41 characters). An empty string removes it.

note.description: One general note for the round.

auto_repair.description: Run the automatic collision repair on the new version (default true).

base_version.description: Version to change; default the latest.

t.description: Moment of the base version's simulation in seconds (0 to its duration).

SavingsInputsState.description: Present on a project only once the time-saved inputs were set (`PUT /projects/{pid}/baseline`).

manual_cycle_s.description: Seconds one person needs per item by hand.

BaselineUpdate.description: Any subset of the fields; send at least one.

limits.description: max_robots 2 to 3, max_reach_m up to 10, max_payload_kg up to 2000, budget_usd 0 or more.

member.description: A fleet member id, or null for the default.

datasheet_url.description: https URL of a datasheet (PDF, HTML or text).

characters.description: Characters of text read from the file.

oneOf.description: Choose your own design. `build` defaults to the project's approved build.

ParsedUrdf.description: The parsed URDF the server attaches to versions and analyses (not part of the stored model).

DesignVersionView.description: A version as served by the API, the stored model plus its parsed URDF.

fleet_parsed.description: Parsed URDF per fleet member id; present only when the version has a fleet.

AnalysisView.description: An analysis as served by the API, the stored model plus its parsed URDF.

QuestionsResult.description: Result of a design job that needs answers.

QuestionsResource.description: The `resource` of a finished design job that asked questions (the questions and the number of the round).

DesignedResult.description: Result of a design job that produced the first version.

VersionResult.description: Result of a revise or fleet_design job.

StudioState.description: Only when the project has at least one studio build.

design_version.description: Must be the approved version; default: the approved version.

base_build.description: Start from this build (its shop alternatives are reused).

pinned.description: Joint name to the alternative id to use for it.

StudioBuildView.description: A build as served by the API, the stored model plus its parsed studio URDF.

StudioBuildResult.description: Result of a studio_build or studio_pdf job.

robot_id.description: The project id; null for `llm_test` and for an `ask` without a project.

result.description: The job's result when `status` is `done`, otherwise null. The shape depends on `kind`.

error.description: The failure message when `status` is `error` or `cancelled`.

error_code.description: Machine-readable cause, for example `datasheet_download`; `cancelled` for a cancelled job.

subject.description: Only in job lists. The candidate id of an analysis, `v<n>` of a revise or fleet design, otherwise null.

resource.description:
With `expand=resource` on a finished job: the result as a full resource. A design that produced a version,
a revise or a fleet_design give the version view (`GET /versions/{n}`); a design with questions gives
`{questions, round}`; a search gives the candidates; an analysis gives the analysis view; a studio_build or studio_pdf gives the build view (`GET /studio/builds/{n}`).
